scheme_name: Construction of Dudhghar/ Godown (Scheduled Caste Area)
description:
The Construction of Dudhghar or Godown scheme is an initiative launched by the Government of India aimed at enhancing the infrastructure for dairy farming in Scheduled Caste areas.

This scheme was introduced under the Ministry of Dairy Development and Fisheries in 2021.

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance for the construction of dairy godowns or Dudhghars.

The scheme aims to improve the storage facilities for milk and milk products in rural areas.

By enhancing storage capacity, the government seeks to increase the income of dairy farmers.

The target beneficiaries of this scheme are primarily Scheduled Caste farmers engaged in dairy farming.

The scheme aims to provide a subsidy of up to 50 percent of the total cost of construction.

The maximum subsidy amount is capped at INR 10 lakh per godown.

The construction of each godown is expected to support the storage of approximately 5,000 liters of milk.

The scheme also aims to promote cooperative dairy farming among Scheduled Caste communities.

Eligible beneficiaries must belong to Scheduled Caste communities as defined by the Government of India.

The age limit for applicants is set at a minimum of 18 years.

There is no specific upper age limit mentioned for eligibility.

The income criteria for eligibility require that the annual income of the applicant should not exceed INR 2 lakh.

Applicants must possess a valid Aadhaar card as proof of identity.

The application process requires the submission of a completed application form.

The application form can be obtained from the local dairy cooperative society or the district dairy development office.

Along with the application form, applicants must submit proof of caste certificate.

A detailed project report outlining the construction plan and estimated costs is also required.

The application must include proof of land ownership or lease agreement for the proposed site.

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the district dairy development officer.

The review process typically takes about 30 days from the date of submission.

If approved, the applicant will receive an approval letter detailing the subsidy amount.

The disbursement of the subsidy is made in two installments.

The first installment of 50 percent is released upon the approval of the project.

The second installment is released after the completion of the construction and inspection by the authorities.

The timeline for the entire process from application to final disbursement can take up to six months.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Dairy Development and Fisheries.

Each state has its own dairy development department responsible for executing the scheme at the state level.

For any queries or assistance, beneficiaries can contact the local dairy development office.

The government also encourages the formation of self-help groups among Scheduled Caste farmers to facilitate the application process.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to uplift the socio-economic status of Scheduled Caste communities.

The government aims to construct at least 5,000 godowns under this scheme in the next five years.

The scheme is expected to benefit over 25,000 Scheduled Caste dairy farmers across the country.

By improving storage facilities, the scheme aims to reduce post-harvest losses of milk.

The initiative is also aligned with the National Dairy Plan which aims to increase milk production in India.

The government has allocated a budget of INR 500 crore for the implementation of this scheme over five years.

The scheme is expected to create employment opportunities in rural areas.

The construction of godowns is anticipated to enhance the quality of milk storage.

This will lead to better prices for dairy farmers in the market.

The scheme also aims to promote the use of modern technology in dairy farming.

Farmers will be encouraged to adopt best practices in milk storage and handling.

The government is also planning to conduct training programs for beneficiaries.

These training programs will cover aspects of dairy farming and management.

The scheme is expected to foster a sense of community among Scheduled Caste farmers.

The government aims to ensure that the benefits reach the intended beneficiaries without any corruption.

Regular audits and inspections will be conducted to monitor the implementation of the scheme.

The scheme is expected to significantly contribute to the economic empowerment of Scheduled Caste communities.

The government has also partnered with various NGOs to facilitate the implementation of the scheme.

These partnerships aim to provide additional support and resources to beneficiaries.

The scheme is a step towards achieving the goal of inclusive growth in rural India.

The government is committed to ensuring that Scheduled Caste farmers have access to necessary resources.

This initiative is part of a larger framework of welfare schemes aimed at marginalized communities.

The scheme reflects the government's focus on improving the livelihoods of dairy farmers.

The construction of Dudhghar or Godown is seen as a critical investment in rural infrastructure.

The government is optimistic about the positive impact of this scheme on dairy production in India.

Overall, the Construction of Dudhghar or Godown scheme is a comprehensive initiative aimed at empowering Scheduled Caste dairy farmers through improved infrastructure and financial support.
